software-engineering.name: Software Engineering
software-engineering.description: Beginner-to-intermediate software engineering learning track. NOT an official UTech curriculum. Covers programming fundamentals, web development, and software engineering practices.

studyGuide.passStrategy: Understand the core idea, type the example yourself, and answer the topic questions before moving to the next level.
studyGuide.masteryStrategy: Build a small project for each level, document decisions and bugs, then continue with the matching FreeCodeCamp course.
studyGuide.notePrompt: Keep a developer notebook: concept, code snippet, error encountered, fix, and what you would improve next time.

levels.title: Programming Fundamentals
levels.description: Core programming concepts every developer must know

topics.title: What Is Programming?
topics.description: Understanding what programming is and how it works
learningObjectives: Know the difference between compilers and interpreters
topics.explanation: Programming is the process of writing instructions that computers can execute. A program is a set of instructions that tells a computer what to do. Source code is the human-readable text that programmers write. This code is then converted to machine code by compilers or executed directly by interpreters.
keyConcepts: Compilers convert entire programs before execution
Interpreters execute code line by line

keyTerms.definition: Set of instructions for a computer

examples.question: Write a simple program that prints 'Hello, World!'
examples.answer: In JavaScript: console.log('Hello, World!'); In Python: print('Hello, World!')
examples.explanation: This is the traditional first program in any language

codeExamples.code:
// This is a simple JavaScript program
console.log('Hello, World!');
codeExamples.explanation: console.log prints text to the console

codeExamples.code:
# This is a simple Python program
print('Hello, World!')

practiceQuestions.question: What is source code?
practiceQuestions.explanation: Source code is what programmers write

commonMistakes: Thinking all languages work the same way
topics.practicalExercise: Write a simple program in any language that prints your name
topics.projectConnection: Understanding programming basics is essential before building any project
studyTips: Run code to see results immediately

topics.title: Computational Thinking
topics.description: Problem-solving approach using computer science concepts
topics.explanation: Computational thinking is a problem-solving approach that breaks complex problems into smaller, manageable parts. It involves four key techniques: decomposition (breaking problems down), pattern recognition (finding similarities), abstraction (focusing on important information), and algorithm design (creating step-by-step solutions).
keyConcepts: Decomposition: break problems into smaller parts

examples.question: How would you decompose building a calculator?
examples.answer: Break into: input handling, operations, display, memory
examples.explanation: Each part can be solved separately

practiceQuestions.question: Breaking a large problem into smaller parts is called:

commonMistakes: Trying to solve everything at once
topics.practicalExercise: Decompose the problem of creating a to-do list application
topics.projectConnection: Computational thinking is used in every project

topics.title: Variables
topics.description: Storing and managing data in programs
topics.explanation: Variables are containers for storing data. They have names that identify them and values that can change during program execution. Constants are like variables but their values cannot change after being set. Good naming makes code readable and maintainable.

keyTerms.definition: Container for data that can change

examples.question: Create a variable to store age
examples.explanation: let for changeable, const for fixed

practiceQuestions.question: Which is used for values that won't change?

topics.practicalExercise: Create variables for different data types and assign values
topics.projectConnection: Variables are used in every program

topics.title: Data Types
topics.explanation: Data types define what kind of data can be stored and how it can be used. Primitive types include strings (text), integers (whole numbers), floating-point numbers (decimals), and booleans (true/false). Complex types include arrays (lists) and objects (records).

codeExamples.code:
let name = 'John'; // string
let age = 25; // integer
let price = 19.99; // float
let isActive = true; // boolean
let fruits = ['apple', 'banana']; // array
let person = { name: 'John', age: 25 }; // object

topics.practicalExercise: Create variables of each data type
topics.projectConnection: Understanding data types is essential for all programming
studyTips: Know when to use each type

topics.title: Operators
topics.explanation: Operators perform operations on values. Arithmetic operators (+, -, *, /) perform calculations. Comparison operators (==, !=, >, <) compare values. Logical operators (&&, ||, !) combine boolean values.

codeExamples.code:
let sum = 5 + 3; // 8
let isEqual = 5 === 5; // true
let andOp = true && false; // false

topics.projectConnection: Operators are used in all logic

topics.title: Conditional Logic
topics.explanation: Conditional logic allows programs to make decisions. The if statement executes code when a condition is true. else executes when false. else-if checks multiple conditions. Nested conditions place conditions inside other conditions.
keyConcepts: if: execute when condition is true
else: execute when condition is false

examples.question: Write code to check if someone can vote (age >= 18)
examples.answer: if (age >= 18) { console.log('Can vote'); } else { console.log('Cannot vote'); }

practiceQuestions.question: What does else execute?
practiceQuestions.explanation: else executes when if condition fails

topics.practicalExercise: Write a program that determines grade based on score
topics.projectConnection: Conditional logic is used in all applications

topics.title: Loops
topics.explanation: Loops repeat code multiple times. For loops repeat a known number of times. While loops repeat while a condition is true. Loop control statements (break, continue) change loop execution.

practiceQuestions.question: Which loop is best for known iterations?
practiceQuestions.explanation: For loops are for known counts

topics.practicalExercise: Write a loop that prints even numbers from 2 to 20

topics.title: Functions
topics.explanation: Functions are reusable blocks of code. They take parameters (inputs), perform operations, and can return values. Functions help organize code, avoid repetition, and make programs more maintainable. Scope determines where variables are accessible.

examples.question: Write a function that adds two numbers
examples.answer: function add(a, b) { return a + b; }
examples.explanation: Parameters a and b, returns sum

practiceQuestions.question: Values passed to a function are called:

topics.practicalExercise: Write functions for basic math operations

topics.title: Input and Output
topics.explanation: Input and output (I/O) allow programs to interact with users and files. Input can come from keyboard, files, or network. Output can go to screen, files, or network. Understanding I/O is essential for building useful applications.
keyConcepts: User input: from keyboard or forms
Program output: to screen or console
Data processing: transform input to output

examples.question: Get user name and print greeting
examples.answer: const name = prompt('Enter name'); console.log('Hello, ' + name);
examples.explanation: Input from prompt, output to console

topics.practicalExercise: Create a program that reads input and displays formatted output

topics.title: Errors
topics.explanation: Errors are problems that occur during program execution. Syntax errors occur when code doesn't follow language rules. Runtime errors occur during execution. Logic errors produce wrong results. Error handling makes programs more robust.

examples.question: What type of error is 'console.lg('hi')'?
examples.explanation: console.lg is not a valid function

practiceQuestions.question: Wrong results from correct code is:

topics.practicalExercise: Create a function with error handling

topics.title: Debugging Fundamentals
topics.explanation: Debugging is the process of finding and fixing bugs. Start by reading error messages carefully. Use console.log to check values. Test assumptions. Use debugger tools. Break problems into smaller parts to isolate issues.
topics.practicalExercise: Debug a program with intentional errors
topics.projectConnection: Debugging is essential for all projects
studyTips: Fix one thing at a time

topics.title: HTML Fundamentals
topics.explanation: HTML (HyperText Markup Language) is the standard language for creating web pages. It uses tags to structure content. Elements consist of opening and closing tags. Attributes provide additional information about elements.
keyConcepts: Elements use opening and closing tags

codeExamples.code:
Hello, World!

This is a paragraph.

topics.projectConnection: HTML is the foundation of web projects

topics.title: Text
topics.explanation: HTML provides various elements for text content. Headings (h1-h6) create hierarchy. Paragraphs (p) contain blocks of text. Strong and em add emphasis. Quotes use blockquote or q. Comments (<!-- -->) document code without displaying.

codeExamples.code:
Main Title

Subtitle

This is a paragraph with emphasis.

commonMistakes: Using headings for styling instead of structure
topics.practicalExercise: Create a document with proper heading hierarchy
topics.projectConnection: Text structure is essential for all web pages
studyTips: Use headings for structure, not styling

topics.title: Links
topics.explanation: Links (anchor tags) connect pages and resources. The href attribute specifies the destination. Internal links point to pages within the same site. External links point to other websites. Navigation menus use multiple links.

examples.question: Create a link to another page

codeExamples.code: Home About External
codeExamples.explanation: Navigation with internal and external links

topics.projectConnection: Navigation is essential for all websites

topics.title: Images
topics.explanation: Images use the img element with src (source) and alt (alternative text) attributes. Alt text describes images for screen readers and when images fail to load. Accessible images are essential for all users.

examples.question: Add an image with alt text
examples.explanation: Image with source and alt text

practiceQuestions.question: Which attribute describes images for screen readers?

topics.practicalExercise: Create a page with multiple images

topics.title: Lists
topics.explanation: HTML supports three list types: ordered lists (ol) with numbers, unordered lists (ul) with bullets, and description lists (dl) for terms and definitions. List items use li elements.

codeExamples.code:
1. First step
  2. Second step
  • Point one
  • Point two

topics.practicalExercise: Create both ordered and unordered lists
topics.projectConnection: Lists organize information in all projects

topics.title: Tables
learningObjectives: Create tables with rows and columns
topics.explanation: Tables display data in rows and columns. The table element contains tr (table rows), th (table headers), and td (table data). Proper headers improve accessibility for screen readers.

codeExamples.code:
Name Age
John 25

topics.practicalExercise: Create a table with student data

topics.title: Forms
topics.explanation: Forms collect user input. Input elements include text fields, checkboxes, radio buttons, and buttons. Labels connect to inputs for accessibility. Validation ensures correct data entry.

codeExamples.code:
<form>
  <label for="name">Name:</label>
  <input type="text" id="name" required>
  
  <label for="email">Email:</label>
  <input type="email" id="email" required>
  
  <button type="submit">Submit</button>
</form>

practiceQuestions.question: Which attribute connects label to input?

topics.title: Semantic HTML
topics.explanation: Semantic HTML uses elements that describe their content. header, nav, main, section, article, aside, and footer provide meaning to page structure. Semantic elements improve accessibility and SEO.

examples.question: Structure a page with semantic elements

codeExamples.code:
My Website

Home

Article Title

Content

Copyright

commonMistakes: Using divs instead of semantic elements
topics.practicalExercise: Convert div-based layout to semantic HTML
topics.projectConnection: Semantic HTML improves all web projects

topics.title: Multimedia
topics.explanation: HTML5 provides audio and video elements for multimedia. Audio plays sound files. Video plays video files with controls. Both support multiple source formats for browser compatibility.

codeExamples.code:
<audio controls>
  <source src="audio.mp3" type="audio/mpeg">
</audio>

<video controls>
  <source src="video.mp4" type="video/mp4">
</video>

topics.practicalExercise: Add audio and video to a page

topics.title: Accessibility
topics.explanation: Accessibility ensures websites work for all users, including those with disabilities. Semantic HTML provides structure. Alt text describes images. Labels connect to inputs. ARIA attributes add additional information for screen readers.

codeExamples.code: Home

practiceQuestions.question: What does alt text do?
practiceQuestions.explanation: Alt text describes images for screen readers

topics.projectConnection: Accessibility is essential for all projects

topics.title: HTML Best Practices
topics.explanation: HTML best practices ensure code is maintainable and performant. Use lowercase tags and attributes. Indent properly. Close all tags. Use semantic elements. Validate HTML. Optimize loading with proper attributes.

examples.question: Write clean HTML
examples.answer: Use semantic elements, proper indentation, and lowercase tags

codeExamples.code:
Title

Title

topics.title: CSS Fundamentals
topics.explanation: CSS (Cascading Style Sheets) styles HTML elements. It uses selectors to target elements, properties to define styles, and values to specify the styling. CSS separates content from presentation.

examples.question: Style all paragraphs red
examples.explanation: Selector p, property color, value red

topics.title: Cascade and Specificity
topics.explanation: The cascade determines which styles apply when multiple rules target the same element. Specificity weights selectors (ID > class > element). Inheritance passes some properties to children. Understanding these concepts prevents styling conflicts.
topics.practicalExercise: Create conflicting rules and understand resolution

topics.title: Box Model
topics.explanation: Every HTML element is a box with content, padding, border, and margin. Content is the actual content. Padding is space inside the border. Border surrounds padding. Margin is space outside the border.
commonMistakes: Not accounting for box model in layout
topics.projectConnection: Box model is fundamental to layout

topics.title: Colors and Backgrounds
topics.explanation: CSS provides multiple ways to specify colors: named colors, hex codes, RGB, HSL. Background properties set background colors, images, and gradients. Color choice affects readability and aesthetics.

topics.title: Typography
topics.explanation: Typography controls text appearance. Font family sets the font. Font size controls text size. Line height affects readability. Text alignment positions text. Good typography improves user experience.

topics.title: Display
topics.explanation: The display property controls how elements are rendered. Block elements take full width. Inline elements flow with text. Inline-block combines both. None hides elements completely.

topics.title: Positioning
topics.explanation: Positioning controls where elements appear. Static is default. Relative shifts from normal position. Absolute positions relative to parent. Fixed positions relative to viewport. Sticky combines relative and fixed.

practiceQuestions.question: Which position is relative to viewport?

topics.practicalExercise: Create fixed header and centered modal

topics.title: Flexbox
topics.explanation: Flexbox is a one-dimensional layout system. It arranges items in rows or columns. Properties control direction, alignment, justification, and wrapping. Flexbox simplifies centering and spacing.

examples.question: Center items horizontally and vertically
examples.answer: display: flex; justify-content: center; align-items: center;

topics.practicalExercise: Create a navigation bar with flexbox
topics.projectConnection: Flexbox is used in all modern layouts

topics.title: CSS Grid
topics.explanation: CSS Grid is a two-dimensional layout system. It arranges items in rows and columns. Grid containers define the layout. Grid items are placed in cells. Grid is ideal for complex layouts.

topics.title: Responsive Design
topics.explanation: Responsive design ensures websites work on all screen sizes. Mobile-first means designing for mobile then enhancing for larger screens. Media queries apply styles based on screen size. Responsive layouts adapt to any device.
topics.projectConnection: Responsive design is essential for all web projects

topics.title: Transitions and Animations
topics.explanation: Transitions smoothly change property values. Animations create complex movements. CSS variables store reusable values. These features add interactivity and polish to interfaces.

topics.title: CSS Architecture
topics.explanation: CSS architecture ensures maintainable styles. Use naming conventions like BEM. Create reusable utility classes. Organize styles by component or feature. Avoid specificity wars and duplicate code.

examples.question: Name a BEM class
examples.explanation: Block: card, Element: title, Modifier: large

topics.title: JavaScript Fundamentals
topics.explanation: JavaScript is the language of the web. It adds interactivity to websites. Modern JavaScript uses let and const for variable declaration. JavaScript has dynamic typing with several data types including strings, numbers, booleans, arrays, and objects.

examples.question: Declare a variable
examples.explanation: let for changeable, const for fixed

topics.practicalExercise: Declare variables of each data type
topics.projectConnection: JavaScript is essential for web development

externalResources.title: JavaScript Algorithms and Data Structures - FreeCodeCamp

topics.title: Functions
topics.explanation: Functions are reusable code blocks. Function declarations use the function keyword. Function expressions assign functions to variables. Arrow functions provide concise syntax. Functions take parameters and return values.

topics.title: Arrays
topics.explanation: Arrays store lists of data. Array methods like map, filter, reduce, and find transform arrays. Map transforms each element. Filter selects matching elements. Reduce combines elements. Find locates specific elements.
topics.practicalExercise: Process a list of numbers using array methods
topics.projectConnection: Arrays process data in all applications

topics.title: Objects
topics.explanation: Objects store key-value pairs. Properties can be accessed with dot or bracket notation. Destructuring extracts properties. Spread syntax copies objects. Objects are fundamental to JavaScript.

topics.title: DOM Manipulation
topics.explanation: The DOM (Document Object Model) represents the page structure. JavaScript can select elements, change their content and styles, and create new elements. DOM manipulation makes pages dynamic.
topics.practicalExercise: Build a dynamic list with DOM manipulation

topics.title: Asynchronous JavaScript
topics.explanation: Asynchronous JavaScript handles operations that take time like API calls. Callbacks are functions passed to other functions. Promises represent future values. Async/await makes async code look synchronous.

practiceQuestions.question: Which makes async code look synchronous?

topics.projectConnection: Async is essential for API calls

topics.title: TypeScript Fundamentals
topics.explanation: TypeScript adds static typing to JavaScript. It catches errors at compile time. Type inference automatically determines types. Type annotations explicitly specify types. TypeScript improves code quality and maintainability.

topics.title: Interfaces and Types
topics.explanation: Interfaces define object shapes. Type aliases create custom types. Union types allow multiple types. Intersection types combine types. These features make TypeScript powerful for defining data structures.

examples.question: Define an interface
examples.answer: interface User { name: string; age: number; }

topics.title: Generics
topics.explanation: Generics create reusable components that work with multiple types. Generic functions accept type parameters. Generic constraints limit what types are allowed. Generics provide type safety with flexibility.

examples.question: Create generic function
examples.answer: function identity<T>(arg: T): T { return arg; }

topics.title: Python Fundamentals
topics.explanation: Python is a readable, versatile language. It uses indentation for code blocks. Variables are dynamically typed. Python has built-in data structures: lists, tuples, sets, and dictionaries. Python is great for beginners and professionals.

codeExamples.code:
# Variables
name = 'John'
age = 25

# Lists
fruits = ['apple', 'banana']
fruits.append('orange')

# Tuples
point = (3, 4)

# Sets
unique_numbers = {1, 2, 3, 3}  # {1, 2, 3}

# Dictionaries
person = {'name': 'John', 'age': 25}

topics.practicalExercise: Create and manipulate Python data structures
topics.projectConnection: Python is used in many applications

topics.title: Functions
topics.explanation: Python functions use the def keyword. Functions take parameters and return values. Python supports default parameters, keyword arguments, and variable arguments. Scope determines variable accessibility.

topics.title: Object-Oriented Programming
topics.explanation: Python supports object-oriented programming. Classes define object blueprints. Objects are class instances. Inheritance allows class extension. Encapsulation protects data. OOP organizes complex programs.

examples.question: Create a class
examples.answer: class Dog: def __init__(self, name): self.name = name

topics.title: Files, APIs, and Databases
topics.explanation: Python handles files with built-in functions. The requests library makes HTTP calls. SQLite provides database access. JSON is used for data exchange. These skills enable data-driven applications.

examples.question: Read a file
examples.answer: with open('file.txt') as f: content = f.read()

codeExamples.code:
# File handling
with open('data.txt', 'w') as f:
    f.write('Hello')

# HTTP request
import requests
response = requests.get('https://api.example.com/data')
data = response.json()

# Database
import sqlite3
conn = sqlite3.connect('app.db')
cursor = conn.cursor()
cursor.execute('CREATE TABLE users (name TEXT)')
cursor.execute('INSERT INTO users VALUES (?)', ('John',))
conn.commit()
conn.close()

practiceQuestions.question: Which library makes HTTP requests?
practiceQuestions.explanation: requests is the standard HTTP library

topics.projectConnection: Data handling is essential for applications

topics.title: Rust Fundamentals
topics.explanation: Rust is a systems programming language focused on safety and performance. Variables are immutable by default. The mut keyword allows mutation. Rust has strict typing with integers, floats, booleans, characters, and tuples.

practiceQuestions.question: Rust variables are:
practiceQuestions.explanation: Rust variables are immutable by default

topics.projectConnection: Rust is used for performance-critical systems

topics.title: Ownership and Borrowing
topics.explanation: Ownership is Rust's most unique feature. Each value has one owner. When owner goes out of scope, value is dropped. Borrowing allows access without ownership. References (&) allow borrowing. This system prevents memory bugs.

topics.title: Structs and Enums
topics.explanation: Structs group related data. Enums define types with variants. Pattern matching (match) handles enum values. Option and Result are important enums for handling optional values and errors.

examples.question: Define a struct
examples.answer: struct User { name: String, age: u32 }

topics.practicalExercise: Create structs and enums for a program

topics.title: Error Handling
topics.explanation: Rust distinguishes between recoverable and unrecoverable errors. Result handles recoverable errors. panic! handles unrecoverable errors. The ? operator propagates errors. Error handling is explicit and safe.

examples.question: Handle a Result
examples.answer: let result = match operation() { Ok(v) => v, Err(e) => return Err(e) };

topics.practicalExercise: Write functions with proper error handling

topics.title: Git Fundamentals
topics.explanation: Git is a version control system that tracks changes to files. It allows collaboration, rollback, and branching. A repository stores project history. Commits save snapshots of changes. Git is essential for software development.

codeExamples.code:
# Initialize repository
git init

# Check status
git status

# Add files to staging
git add .

# Commit changes
git commit -m "Initial commit"

# View history
git log

topics.practicalExercise: Initialize a repository and make commits
topics.projectConnection: Git is essential for all projects

topics.title: Branches and Merging
topics.explanation: Branches allow parallel development. The main branch is the primary branch. Feature branches isolate new work. Merging combines branches. Merge conflicts occur when changes overlap and must be resolved.

examples.question: Create and switch to a branch
examples.explanation: Create and switch in one command

codeExamples.code:
# Create branch
git branch feature-branch

# Switch to branch
git checkout feature-branch

# Create and switch
git checkout -b another-branch

# Merge branch to main
git checkout main
git merge feature-branch

# Delete branch
git branch -d feature-branch

topics.practicalExercise: Create feature branches and merge them

topics.title: GitHub Collaboration
topics.explanation: GitHub hosts remote Git repositories. Push uploads local changes. Pull downloads remote changes. Pull requests propose changes for review. Issues track work. Code reviews improve quality.

codeExamples.code:
# Clone repository
git clone https://github.com/user/repo.git

# Add remote
git remote add origin https://github.com/user/repo.git

# Push changes
git push origin main

# Pull changes
git pull origin main

topics.practicalExercise: Create a GitHub repository and push code

topics.title: Data Structures Fundamentals
topics.explanation: Data structures organize and store data efficiently. Arrays store contiguous elements. Linked lists use pointers. Stacks and queues are linear structures. Hash tables provide fast lookup. Trees and graphs represent relationships.

practiceQuestions.question: Which is LIFO?
practiceQuestions.explanation: Stack is Last In First Out

topics.projectConnection: Data structures are fundamental to programming

topics.title: Linked Lists
topics.explanation: Linked lists store elements in nodes with pointers to next nodes. They allow efficient insertion and deletion. Unlike arrays, they don't require contiguous memory. Each node contains data and a reference to the next node.

examples.question: Advantage of linked list over array?

topics.projectConnection: Linked lists are used in many applications

topics.title: Trees and Graphs
topics.explanation: Trees are hierarchical structures with root and children. Binary trees have at most two children per node. Binary search trees maintain sorted order. Graphs are networks of nodes connected by edges.

examples.question: What is the top node of a tree?

topics.projectConnection: Trees are used in databases and file systems

topics.title: Algorithm Fundamentals
topics.explanation: Algorithms are step-by-step procedures for solving problems. They can be expressed in pseudocode or flowcharts. Good algorithms are correct, efficient, and clear. Algorithm design involves problem decomposition and pattern recognition.

examples.question: Write pseudocode for finding maximum
examples.answer: max = arr[0]; for each element: if element > max: max = element

topics.title: Searching Algorithms
topics.explanation: Linear search checks each element sequentially. Binary search repeatedly divides sorted arrays. Linear search is O(n). Binary search is O(log n). Binary search requires sorted data.
commonMistakes: Using binary search on unsorted data
topics.projectConnection: Searching is used in all applications

topics.title: Sorting Algorithms
topics.explanation: Sorting algorithms arrange elements in order. Bubble sort repeatedly swaps adjacent elements. Selection sort finds minimum each pass. Insertion sort builds sorted array. Merge sort divides and conquers. Quick sort uses pivots.
topics.projectConnection: Sorting is fundamental to data processing

topics.title: Algorithm Complexity
topics.explanation: Big O notation describes algorithm efficiency. O(1) is constant time. O(log n) is logarithmic. O(n) is linear. O(n²) is quadratic. Space complexity measures memory usage. Understanding complexity helps choose algorithms.

examples.question: What is complexity of loop through array?

externalResources.title: JavaScript Algorithms and Data Structures - FreeCodeCamp

topics.title: Database Fundamentals
topics.explanation: Databases store and organize data systematically. Relational databases use tables with rows and columns. Primary keys uniquely identify records. Foreign keys establish relationships. Databases provide efficient data retrieval and management.
keyConcepts: Tables: data organized in rows and columns

examples.question: What uniquely identifies a record?
examples.explanation: Primary key is unique for each record

topics.title: SQL
topics.explanation: SQL (Structured Query Language) manipulates database data. SELECT retrieves data. INSERT adds records. UPDATE modifies records. DELETE removes records. JOIN combines data from multiple tables.
topics.practicalExercise: Write SQL queries for a database
topics.projectConnection: SQL is essential for data-driven apps

topics.title: Database Design
topics.explanation: Database design ensures efficient, reliable databases. Normalization reduces data redundancy. Indexes speed up queries. Transactions ensure data consistency. Security protects sensitive data. Good design prevents problems.

topics.title: API Fundamentals
topics.explanation: APIs (Application Programming Interfaces) allow applications to communicate. HTTP methods define operations: GET retrieves, POST creates, PUT updates, DELETE removes. Status codes indicate results. JSON is the common data format.
keyConcepts: HTTP methods: GET, POST, PUT, DELETE
Status codes: 200 success, 404 not found, 500 error

externalResources.title: Back End Development and APIs - FreeCodeCamp

topics.title: API Authentication
topics.explanation: API authentication verifies users. API keys identify applications. Tokens authenticate users. Sessions maintain state. CORS controls access. Security prevents unauthorized access. Authentication is essential for protected endpoints.
topics.projectConnection: Security is essential for all APIs

topics.title: Testing Fundamentals
topics.explanation: Software testing ensures quality and correctness. Unit testing tests individual components. Integration testing tests component interaction. System testing tests complete system. Acceptance testing verifies requirements. Testing prevents bugs.

topics.title: Test Coverage and Mocking
topics.explanation: Test coverage measures how much code is tested. Mocking replaces dependencies with test doubles. Assertions verify expected behavior. Good tests are clear, independent, and maintainable. Coverage helps identify untested code.

topics.title: Debugging Fundamentals
topics.explanation: Debugging is finding and fixing bugs. Read error messages carefully. Use console logging to check values. Set breakpoints to pause execution. Step through code to understand flow. Systematic debugging finds issues faster.
topics.projectConnection: Debugging is essential for all development
studyTips: Fix one thing at a time

topics.title: Debugging Strategies
topics.explanation: Effective debugging follows a workflow: reproduce, isolate, fix, verify. Browser DevTools provides powerful debugging. Different environments require different approaches. Logging and monitoring help in production. Performance debugging finds bottlenecks.
keyConcepts: Debugging workflow: reproduce, isolate, fix, verify

topics.title: Software Engineering Fundamentals
topics.explanation: Software engineering is the systematic approach to developing software. The Software Development Life Cycle (SDLC) includes requirements, design, implementation, testing, deployment, and maintenance. Methodologies like Agile and Scrum guide development processes.
keyConcepts: SDLC: requirements, design, implement, test, deploy, maintain

examples.question: What is SDLC?
examples.answer: Software Development Life Cycle - systematic process

codeExamples.code:
SDLC Phases:
1. Requirements Gathering
2. Analysis
3. Design
4. Implementation
5. Testing
6. Deployment
7. Maintenance

topics.practicalExercise: Plan a software project using SDLC
topics.projectConnection: Software engineering principles guide all projects

topics.title: Requirements
topics.explanation: Requirements define what software must do. Functional requirements describe features. Non-functional requirements describe quality attributes. User stories describe features from user perspective. Use cases describe interactions.

examples.question: Write a user story
examples.answer: As a user, I want to login so I can access my account
examples.explanation: User story format: As a, I want, so that

codeExamples.code:
User Story Format:
As a [user type]
I want [feature]
So that [benefit]

Example:

topics.title: Software Design
topics.explanation: Software design creates the blueprint for implementation. Architecture defines high-level structure. Frontend and backend are separated concerns. APIs connect them. Clean code principles ensure maintainability. Design patterns solve common problems.

codeExamples.code:
Architecture Layers:
┌─────────────┐
│  Frontend   │ (HTML, CSS, JS)
├─────────────┤
│    API      │ (REST endpoints)
├─────────────┤
│   Backend   │ (Business logic)
├─────────────┤
│  Database   │ (Data storage)
└─────────────┘

topics.title: Security Fundamentals
topics.explanation: Software security protects data and users. Authentication verifies identity. Authorization controls access. Encryption protects data. Secure coding prevents vulnerabilities. Security must be considered throughout development.
topics.projectConnection: Security is essential for all applications

topics.title: Agile Development
topics.explanation: Agile is an iterative development approach. Scrum uses sprints, daily standups, and retrospectives. Kanban uses visual boards. Agile values working software, collaboration, and responding to change over rigid processes.

codeExamples.code:
Scrum Events:
- Sprint Planning (start of sprint)
- Daily Standup (15 min daily)
- Sprint Review (end of sprint)
- Sprint Retrospective (improvement)

Kanban Board:
┌──────────┬──────────┬──────────┐
│ To Do    │ In Progress│ Done    │
├──────────┼──────────┼──────────┤
│ Task 1   │ Task 3   │ Task 5   │
│ Task 2   │ Task 4   │          │
└──────────┴──────────┴──────────┘

topics.title: CI/CD and Deployment
topics.explanation: CI/CD automates software delivery. Continuous Integration merges code frequently. Continuous Deployment automates releases. Deployment moves code to production. Monitoring tracks performance. Maintenance keeps software running.

codeExamples.code:
# GitHub Actions CI/CD
deploy:
  runs-on: ubuntu-latest
  steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@v2
    - name: Install dependencies
      run: npm install
    - name: Run tests
      run: npm test
    - name: Build
      run: npm run build
    - name: Deploy
      run: npm run deploy

topics.title: Refactoring and Technical Debt
topics.explanation: Refactoring improves code without changing behavior. Technical debt accumulates from shortcuts. Clean code is readable and maintainable. Regular refactoring prevents debt accumulation. Code review helps maintain quality.

examples.question: Improving code without changing behavior is?

topics.title: Beginner Projects
topics.explanation: Beginner projects build foundational skills. Start with simple applications like calculators and to-do lists. Each project reinforces programming concepts. Projects provide practical experience. Build projects to learn effectively.

topics.title: Intermediate Projects
topics.explanation: Intermediate projects integrate multiple technologies. Weather apps use APIs. Trackers use databases. Full-stack applications combine frontend and backend. These projects demonstrate professional skills.

topics.title: Final Project: Student Study Application
topics.explanation: The final project combines all skills: requirements, planning, Git, frontend, backend, database, APIs, authentication, testing, debugging, documentation, deployment, and maintenance. This project demonstrates complete software engineering competence.

codeExamples.code:
Project Structure:
├── frontend/       (Svelte/React)
│   ├── src/
│   └── public/
├── backend/        (Node/Python)
│   ├── routes/
│   └── models/
├── database/       (SQL schema)
├── tests/          (unit, integration)
├── docs/           (documentation)
└── deploy/         (CI/CD config)
